title: Denise C NDE 5143
content: Well, it was the winter of 1977. I was sick with pneumonia, and we had just had a blizzard. My dad was away on a business trip. My mom had to go to the basement to get something. I went into the kitchen, and I heard my mom call up to me to take my cough medicine. I went to take it, and I felt my body fall in slow motion. I heard my head hit the floor. My mom yelled up to me,' Is everything okay?' I felt that if I answered her, I would die. I felt like a battery that needed to be recharged. My mom ran upstairs and saw me lying on the kitchen floor. She yelled to my four-year-old sister, 'Melissa! Mommy needs your help! Something is wrong with Denise!' I was aware of my mom carrying me and putting me on the sofa. She told my sister to sit on the floor and to not let her sister fall off the sofa. My mom went to call the ambulance, but our phone was out due to the blizzard. She was wearing her pajamas, bathrobe, and slippers, and she ran across the street without a coat. Our street wasn't plowed yet. It took the ambulance about an hour to get to our house, even though the hospital was only six miles away from our house. I was dead. I'm not sure for how long. I was at one end of a tunnel and I saw a group of people at the other end of it. From the background, a strong light was emanating, outlining the crowd with a beautiful yellow light. I could not see any of their faces - it was too dark. Two of the men, I knew, were my Irish grandfather's brothers. I could tell that's who they were because they were wearing the same type of hat my grandfather wore - those wool hats from the 1930s and 1940s. Then, I believe, Jesus spoke to me. It was such an incredible voice! The voice said, 'DENISE! GO BACK! IT'S NOT YOUR TIME YET!' This voice had the sound of every good and kind comment that had ever been made to me. Then I felt an electrical feeling, like a surge of energy rushing through me.

arrival.religious_figure_detail: Jesus spoke: 'DENISE! GO BACK! IT'S NOT YOUR TIME YET!'
arrival.other_being_detail: Group of people at the other end of the tunnel; two men identified as her Irish grandfather's brothers, recognized by their wool hats from the 1930s and 1940s; faces not visible because it was too dark.

environment.environment_other_detail: Strong light emanating from the background, outlining the crowd with a beautiful yellow light; faces were too dark to see.

boundary_and_return.return_method_other_detail: Felt an electrical feeling, like a surge of energy rushing through her.

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Pneumonia; collapsed at home during a blizzard; ambulance delayed about an hour.

stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: Narrative begins with physical collapse and awareness of events in the home, then tunnel with a group of people and bright light, then a directive to return and an electrical surge upon return.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: She felt that if she answered her mother, she would die; described feeling like a battery that needed to be recharged; return accompanied by an electrical surge of energy.
unique_elements.notable_quotes: 'DENISE! GO BACK! IT'S NOT YOUR TIME YET!'
